  "cut_point": "We are given:

m > n \geq 1
$$
and we need to find the **smallest value of $ m + n $** such that:

$$
1000 \mid 1978^m - 1978^n
$$

$$
1978^m \equiv 1978^n \pmod{1000}

---

### Step 1: Simplify the congruence

We can factor out $ 1978^n $:

$$
1978^m - 1978^n = 1978^n(1978^{m - n} - 1)
$$

So the congruence becomes:

$$
1978^n(1978^{m - n} - 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{1000}
$$

This implies:

$$
1978^{m - n} \equiv 1 \pmod{1000}
$$",

annotation.cut_point:
We are given:

$$
m > n \geq 1
$$
and we need to find the **smallest value of $ m + n $** such that:

$$
1000 \mid 1978^m - 1978^n
$$

This means:

$$
1978^m \equiv 1978^n \pmod{1000}
$$

---

### Step 1: Simplify the congruence

We can factor out $ 1978^n $:

$$
1978^m - 1978^n = 1978^n(1978^{m - n} - 1)
$$

So the congruence becomes:

$$
1978^n(1978^{m - n} - 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{1000}
$$

This implies:

$$
1978^{m - n} \equiv 1 \pmod{1000}
$$
